note: [agent-bulk] nuecc, 7 showers, 12 segments. Verdict shower 16014 (pdg 11, kine_charge 145.6, kine_best 102.2 MeV, 1 seg, len 35.5). CORRECTION 17: 16014 is the SECOND entry of the kine_charge-ordered list and the first with pdg==11. I passed over 16012 (pdg 13, kine_charge 275.1 / kine_best 382.4 MeV, 5 segments, 159.7 cm), the highest-energy object in the event; its own cmp_div is 0.0-143.1 cm at 0.0-10.4 deg, i.e. a long narrow chain, and I make no verdict on it -- but see the closing remark, because it bears on what this event is. CORRECTION 6, READ THIS FIRST: this is a PID verdict and the event therefore carries NO clustering judgement. On clustering grounds I found nothing wrong in either direction and want that on the record: 16014 has exactly one member (nseg 1, owner-grouped count 1, cmp_div says 1 segment(s) plotted at distance 0.0-0.0 cm, angle 0.0-0.0 deg -- the triple-check of correction 16 is trivially satisfied), so nothing foreign was swallowed; and every other segment in the event sits at 80.9-85.8 deg from its axis except 21015 (1.3 MeV, 34.1 cm out at 151.0 deg, i.e. behind the start) and 16012/16020 which touch it at the vertex, so there is no contiguous unclaimed charge anywhere in its cone to add. VERTEX IS GOOD and proven from the polylines, not eyeballed: three segments have a point at exactly 0.0 cm from the main vertex -- 16012 (23.8 cm, pdg 13), 16014 (35.5 cm) itself, and 16020 (1.9 cm, pdg 211, correctly unowned). Judged from vtxz-az-055-el+20 (correction 20: vtxz-* written automatically, event_half_span 180.2 cm, r95 144.2 cm), which shows a clean two-prong star with both prongs leaving the star itself. WHY THIS IS A PID VERDICT: on shw16014-az-055-el+20 the entire shower is ONE straight thin line running 35.5 cm from the vertex with a small hook at the far end -- no cone, no opening angle, no branching, and a blob point cloud whose width is indistinguishable from that of the neighbouring 16012 track in the same frame. 35.5 cm is about 2.5 radiation lengths in argon (X0 = 14 cm); a 146 MeV electron would have branched and widened well inside that, and this object does neither. The pilot's counter-argument on evt175896, that an electron starts as a narrow MIP stem for about one radiation length, does not rescue this one at 2.5 X0. Nor can this be a real electron whose shower charge was simply lost by clustering, because there IS no unclaimed charge downstream of its end to lose -- the five scope-skipped showers are 1.3 to 7.7 MeV fragments at 34 to 216 cm from the vertex, none of them in front of 16014. Supporting arithmetic, offered as corroboration only and NOT as the basis (correction 18): the usual trap does not bite here because 16014 is a single 60-point polyline that covers the whole object, so skeleton length is not under-covering blob extent. Converting to the track convention first with the display's own shower-to-track ratio (this event shows no such line, so I used the 154.2/256.3 = 0.60 printed on evt318769) gives roughly 87 MeV over 35.5 cm, about 2.5 MeV/cm, i.e. near MIP. That is consistent with the shape, and the verdict would stand without it. ONE THING FOR THE OWNER: this is labelled nuecc, and neither prong looks like an electron -- 16014 is a 35.5 cm MIP-like line and 16012 is a 159.7 cm narrow chain spanning 143 cm at under 10.4 deg, which is far too long for a 380 MeV EM shower (shower maximum is around 5 X0, some 70 cm). So the event may have no reconstructed EM shower at all rather than a mis-shaped one. I am not making that a verdict: 16012 is pdg 13 and out of scope for the verdict radio under correction 17. PI0: no reco group, both pio_id -1, kine_div says no pi0 group in this event and no pio-*.png was written; no pairing proposed. drag_check both true, probe_radius 87.6 px, probe_degenerate false.
